chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorced his wife once, then took her back before her waiting period expired, and did not bear witness to his taking her back. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is his wife as long as her waiting period has not expired, and it was befitting for him to bear witness to his taking her back. So if he was ignorant of that, let him bear witness when he knows, and I do not see any harm in what he has done. And indeed, many of the people, if they wanted proof for their marriages today, would not find anyone to establish the testimony regarding their matter, and I do not see any harm in what he has done, and if he bears witness, that is better.'

key_terms.رَجْعَتِهَا: Revocation of divorce / taking back the wife
key_terms.يُشْهِدْ: To bear witness / to appoint witnesses

ai.seo_question: Is a revocation of divorce (raj'a) valid without witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) ruled that a man who divorces his wife once and then takes her back before her waiting period (iddah) expires without witnesses is still married to her. While bearing witness is recommended (mustahabb) and befitting, the marriage remains valid even if he was ignorant of this requirement, though doing so is better.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who divorces his wife, then reverts back to her before she fulfils her waiting period, and does not keep a witness upon his reversion. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is his wife for as long as her waiting period is not fulfilled, and it would have been befitting for him if he kept a witness upon his reversion to her. So if he was ignorant of that, so let him keep a witness when he knows, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not see any problem with what he has done; and that a lot of the people, if the proof was wanted upon their marriages, they would not find anyone who would affirm the testimony upon what was from their matters, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not see any problem with that which he has done, and if he were to keep witnesses, so it would be better’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who divorces his wife, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Although it is proper to arrange for witness about one’s going back to one’s wife before the expiration of waiting period, but if one is ignorant one should arrange for witness when he comes to know. However, I do not see any harm in what he has done. Many people, when in need of witnesses, at the time of marriage do not find witnesses for what has happened about their affair. I do not see anything harmful in it but if one finds witness it is better.’”
